newsitem.title: INDIA: Sri Lanka president in surprise Delhi visit.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka president in surprise Delhi visit.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga was expected in New Delhi on Tuesday possibly to hold talks with Indian leaders over her country's ethnic war with Tamil rebels, official sources said.

Indian newspapers said Kumaratunga's surprise visit follows reports of an offer by the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) to hold peace talks with her government through unidentified mediators.
"The president was due to arrive. She may have arrived already," one source told Reuters.
A Sri Lankan official said his embassy would "make a statement on this matter later", but declined to say more. "We cannot comment on this for security reasons," another Sri Lankan official said.
The Indian Express newspaper said: "Amid reports of impending negotiations with the LTTE through mediators President Kumaratunga leaves for New Delhi on Tuesday."

The Hindu newspaper said Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Laxman Kadirgamar who had arrived in New Delhi for a ministerial meeting of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation last week was still in New Delhi.
